title: A former journalist turned Bengaluru's trash problem into a business that recovers 96% of what it handles
sources: YourStory, 2026 - Wilma Rodrigues on waste as a resource, not a liability
Oko-Institut - Waste Management in India: A Woman Fights for the Circular Economy
caption:
Wilma Rodrigues was a Mumbai journalist with no background in waste management. She moved to Bengaluru in 2000 and built one of India's biggest circular-economy businesses anyway.

In 2001, Rodrigues started Saahas, a nonprofit helping implement India's first municipal solid waste rules on the ground in Bengaluru. In 2013, she spun that work into Saahas Zero Waste, a for-profit circular-economy business managing waste for companies and institutions.

In the last financial year, Saahas Zero Waste recovered over 96% of the waste it handled as a resource instead of sending it to a landfill.

She didn't wait for someone else to fix the waste problem. She built the company that treats trash like a resource instead.
